contract: Protection ON defaults to protected copies; OFF keeps existing display-envelope/format semantics. Explicit plaintext is per artifact, with no global preference, password or confirmation in the normal path.

One host prepare/validate boundary binds full authoritative source, policy and mapping state before formatting and clipping. Metadata, JSON keys and filenames are included. Failed validation never falls back to raw originals.

Session copy loads the canonical session. Raw stream provenance is captured outside event text and grants scanning only, never alias restoration. Default protected copies explicitly withhold unknown raw origins; ON memory copies explicitly withhold unprovable memory origins.

Memory entry text remains its own stored authority, including active expired records and historical origins whose original thread has been deleted. Scan each complete entry against its actual source scopes, then the assembled payload against the steward scope.

Final synchronous guards bind session write sequence, memory writer epoch/config generation, policy and persisted mapping file identity. Policy guard starts before readConfig await and spans bounded retries.
LRU never evicts dirty/pending scopes. Multi-source guards retain metadata rather than entire mappings. Proofs are one use, 60 seconds, maximum four and an estimated 64 MiB retained-payload budget.
Browser prepares Blob, validates or replaces dirty artifact with bounded retry, checks known source/config state and downloads synchronously. Response-to-OS submission gap is explicitly retained.

limitations: Synthetic local receiver and fixture vault do not prove live-provider/platform delivery, actual Windows DPAPI export latency, peak process memory or full release-package acceptance.
File-identity and generation guards cover application writers and ordinary external edits, not malicious same-account OS isolation or forged filesystem metadata.
Browser final validation response and OS file submission are separate processes; already downloaded copies cannot be revoked.
Explicit plaintext is a deliberate user copy; unproven/foreign memory alias material can still be omitted with a visible notice. Raw source identifiers never grant private restoration.
Mermaid source/SVG/PNG and other channels are not covered by this batch. Independent namespace and ASR remain paused; M2-5 is cancelled.
